patients.summary: Elementary art teacher who joined in 2021 with undiagnosed bloody diarrhea; colonoscopy first called it ulcerative colitis, later revised to Crohn disease with a perianal fistula, treated with mesalamine, two prednisone courses and infliximab. Iron deficiency anemia and dietary B12 deficiency on a vegan diet, three bouts of erythema nodosum, and a 2025 admission for small bowel obstruction from a fibrotic ileal stricture managed without surgery.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 27 y/o woman looking for a new primary care home; her old office stopped taking her plan's tier. Teaches art at an elementary school, needs late-afternoon or school-vacation slots when possible. Main concern: blood in her stool on and off since around the holidays, with cramping and some weight loss. Denies passing out, vomiting blood or severe pain right now. Advised that if bleeding gets heavy, she gets lightheaded, or pain becomes severe she should go to the ED. Booked new patient visit April 20, 9:00. Sent the records release form to her email.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: establishing care; blood with bowel movements since about December.

HPI: 27 y/o elementary art teacher. Roughly 4 months of loose stools, on bad days 4-5 a day, some nights she wakes to go. Bright red blood mixed in more often than not. Crampy lower belly pain before BMs that eases after. Her jeans are looser; she thinks she is down several pounds since fall without trying. No fevers she has measured. No travel, no antibiotics before this started, no one at home sick. She has not had a colonoscopy or seen GI. She switched to a fully vegan diet late last year and wondered at first if that was the cause.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none, no supplements. Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: father has Crohn disease. Mother rheumatoid arthritis. Paternal aunt hypothyroid.
Social: lives alone in an apartment in town. Smoked about a pack a day for 10 years, quit in October, using no nicotine now. Drinks 1-2 a month. Vegan since late 2020.

ROS: + fatigue, mild. No chest pain, no syncope, no rash, no joint swelling, no urinary symptoms.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thin-appearing but well. Conjunctivae slightly pale. Mouth: no ulcers. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nondistended, no mass, no organomegaly. Rectal deferred to GI. Skin without rash. Joints without swelling.

A/P:
1. Chronic bloody diarrhea with weight loss in a 27 y/o with a father who has Crohn disease. Inflammatory bowel disease is the main concern. CBC, CMP today. Referral to GI placed as urgent; she knows to call or go in for heavy bleeding, fever or severe pain.
2. Possible anemia (pale conjunctivae) - CBC today. Iron studies once GI has seen her.
3. Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 6 months ago. Congratulated. No cessation aids needed.
4. Health maintenance: requesting old records (Pap, vaccines). PHQ-2 1.

RTC after GI visit, about 2-3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Deborah, your blood count shows anemia. With the bleeding you described, that fits with blood loss, and it is one more reason to get you in with GI soon. Your kidney and liver tests look fine; albumin is at the low end of normal. Once GI has seen you we will check your iron levels at a follow-up here. GI's office should call you this week; let us know if you have not heard by Monday.

reports.text: Specimen adequate for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 14 pages from her previous primary care office. Abstracted:
- Pap July 2019: negative (NILM).
- HPV vaccine series x3 completed 2007-2008.
- Tdap August 2016.
- COVID vaccine (Pfizer) 2/13/21 and 3/6/21, given at the school district's staff clinic; card copy included.
- Problem list at that office: none. Meds: none. NKDA.
Entered into immunization record. Original pages scanned under Media.

events.reason: Bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss

conditions.label: Ulcerative colitis
conditions.note: Rectum to splenic flexure, with pseudopolyps

medications.drug_text: mesalamine 800 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily

results.test: C. difficile toxin A and B

reports.text: Indication: hematochezia, diarrhea, weight loss. Moderate sedation. Prep good. Scope advanced to the cecum; terminal ileum intubated and normal over the examined length. From the rectum proximally to the splenic flexure the mucosa is continuously inflamed: erythema, loss of vascular pattern, friability and scattered ulcerations, with several swollen pseudopolyps. The colon proximal to the splenic flexure is normal. Biopsies taken from the involved segments and from the right colon.
reports.conclusion: Continuous colitis from the rectum to the splenic flexure with pseudopolyps, consistent with ulcerative colitis. Biopsies pending.

reports.text:
A. Rectum and sigmoid, biopsies: colonic mucosa with chronic active inflammation, crypt distortion and crypt abscesses; the inflammation is confined to the mucosa and submucosa. No granulomas. No dysplasia.
B. Descending colon, biopsies: similar changes.
C. Right colon, biopsies: colonic mucosa without significant abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Chronic colitis limited to mucosa and submucosa, distal colon; right colon unremarkable. No dysplasia.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation and colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 06/03/2021
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for sending Ms. Shapiro, 27, for evaluation of rectal bleeding.

She describes about six months of intermittent bloody diarrhea with crampy abdominal pain and weight loss. At worst she has six bowel movements a day and is getting up at night to go. No fevers. No prior GI evaluation. Recent stool culture and C. diff toxin, sent by our office the week before, were negative.

PMH: none prior to this. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with Crohn disease; mother RA.
SH: former smoker (1 ppd x 10 years, quit 10/2020). Rare alcohol. Teacher.

Exam: well-appearing. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant, no rebound, no guarding. No perianal disease.

Labs today: Hgb 10.2, ESR 45, CRP 25 mg/L, albumin 3.2.

Colonoscopy (same day): continuous inflammation with ulceration from the rectum to the splenic flexure, pseudopolyps, normal proximal colon and terminal ileum. Pathology (resulted 6/8): chronic colitis confined to the mucosa and submucosa, no granulomas.

Impression: ulcerative colitis, left-sided. Anemia, likely blood loss plus inflammation.

Plan:
- Mesalamine DR 800 mg PO three times daily; prescription sent.
- Expect improvement over 4-8 weeks; call for worsening bleeding, fever or more than 8 stools a day.
- Anemia: suggest iron studies with her PCP once the colitis settles.
- Follow up with us in about 6 months, sooner as needed.

Allergies: NKDA.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI consult received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: GI consult letter, colonoscopy and pathology for 6/3 received by fax and routed to PCP. PCP reviewed: ulcerative colitis, on mesalamine from GI; add to problem list; anemia follow-up visit here in August as planned. Pt notified that we have the records.

documents.title: Question about new medication
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, GI started me on mesalamine three times a day. School is out in a couple weeks but right now the midday dose is hard because I'm in the classroom straight through lunch some days. Is it OK to take it at like 7, 3 and 10 instead of with meals? Also is it vegan? Sorry, weird question. Thanks, Deborah

documents.title: RE: Question about new medication
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not a weird question at all. Spacing it 7 am, 3 pm and bedtime is fine; the tablets can be taken with or without food, just swallow them whole. The inactive ingredients vary by manufacturer - your pharmacist can check the brand they stock. If GI wants a different schedule they will tell you, but this works. Glad you got in to see them.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Deborah, we missed you at your follow-up on Tuesday afternoon. Please call or reply here to reschedule; the doctor would like to recheck your blood count and iron. Patient replied same day: so sorry, teacher setup week, totally forgot. Will call once the school year settles.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Walk-in for seasonal flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions. Quadrivalent flu given IM left deltoid, lot recorded. VIS given. Tolerated well. Reminded her she is overdue for her anemia follow-up; she says she feels more tired lately and will book this week.

events.reason: Fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, dizziness

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (65 mg elemental iron) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for the overdue anemia visit. For about 2 months she has been wiped out by the end of the school day, short of breath climbing the two flights to her classroom, and gets dizzy standing up from the floor after working with the kids. No chest pain, no fainting. Bowels: much better since GI started mesalamine in June, 1-2 formed BMs most days, rare streak of blood. Still strictly vegan, now about a year, and takes no vitamins or supplements. Periods regular, not heavy.

Meds: mesalamine DR 800 mg TID (GI). NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted, weight down a bit from April. Pale skin and pale conjunctivae. Heart: regular, soft systolic murmur at the left sternal border, not heard in April. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

Labs drawn this morning (resulted at 1 pm): Hgb 9.2, MCV 74. Iron 30, TIBC 600, ferritin 8. B12 in range, toward the low end. Folate normal.

A/P:
1. Iron deficiency anemia, microcytic - from colitis blood loss plus a vegan diet with little absorbable iron. Start ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental) once daily. No need to separate it from the mesalamine; keep it away from tea/coffee and with vitamin C if she can. Recheck CBC and ferritin in 2 months. Discussed IV iron if she cannot tolerate pills or does not respond.
2. Systolic murmur - soft, flow-type with Hgb of 9; listen again once the anemia corrects.
3. Ulcerative colitis - improved on mesalamine, followed by GI.
4. Vegan diet - B12 low-normal; talked about a B12 source. Recheck at her physical.
5. COVID booster given today.

RTC 2 months. ED if chest pain, fainting or heavy bleeding.

documents.title: Iron teaching call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt per PCP to review iron. Take 1 tab daily, ideally on an empty stomach or with a small amount of food if it upsets her stomach; avoid taking with coffee or tea; stools may turn dark green or black from the iron, which is expected - but red blood or tarry, sticky stools with dizziness should be reported. Constipation is common; increase fluids. She picked it up last night. Questions answered. Lab recheck to be scheduled for late January.

documents.title: Iron question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doctor, quick question. I've been taking the iron every morning with orange juice like the nurse said. My stomach is a little crampy for an hour after but it passes. Is it OK to switch to night? I'm on break now and noticing it more. Also feeling less dizzy on the stairs already!

documents.title: RE: Iron question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, bedtime is fine, and taking it with a small snack is OK if the cramping bothers you. Great to hear the stairs are easier. See you in late January with labs.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: iron deficiency anemia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Iron f/u. Taking ferrous sulfate nightly, missed a few doses over break. Energy clearly better, stairs at school no longer winding her, dizziness gone. Some constipation, manageable. Colitis quiet - formed stools, no blood in weeks. Still vegan.

Vitals as charted. Color better. Heart regular, murmur not appreciated today. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender.

Labs this AM: Hgb and ferritin both up from November, still below normal. MCV rising.

A/P: IDA responding to oral iron. Continue daily. Recheck CBC/iron at the physical in May. B12 then too. UC per GI, on mesalamine.
Physical in May.

documents.title: Lab copies
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could you post my January blood counts so I can show my GI at the next visit? I'd like to keep my own folder of results.

documents.title: RE: Lab copies
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Deborah, your January CBC and iron results are now released in the Results section of the portal, and we faxed a copy to your GI office as well.

documents.title: Refill: ferrous sulfate
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting refill of ferrous sulfate 325 mg, #90. On med list, last OV 1/25/22. Approved per protocol with 1 refill.

reports.text: Liquid-based preparation. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL - 28F

Interval: doing well overall. Energy much improved on iron. For the last few weeks her stools have been looser again, 2-3 a day, no blood, no night waking. She sent GI a message and they said to keep the mesalamine going and call if it worsens; next GI visit is in the fall.
Diet: vegan, no B12 or other supplement still. Exercise: walks most evenings.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap 2019 normal - due today.
Mood fine, PHQ-9 2. Former smoker, no relapse. Alcohol rare.

Current meds: mesalamine DR 800 mg TID (GI); ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.
FH: father Crohn disease, mother RA, paternal aunt hypothyroidism.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal, no oral ulcers. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap collected. Skin clear, shins normal. Joints normal. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance: Pap today. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening today. Lipids. Tdap 2016, current. COVID vaccinated with booster. Flu in the fall.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC, iron studies today. Continue iron.
3. Ulcerative colitis - mild loosening of stools, GI aware; she will call them if bleeding or more frequent stools.
4. Vegan diet - B12 today; she would rather take a pill than injections if low.

Will message results.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (1000 mcg) by mouth daily

documents.title: Lab results: B12 low
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. B12 182, low (was low-normal in November) - dietary, from a strict vegan diet with no supplement. No numbness, tingling, balance trouble or memory change per her. Hgb now in the normal range and ferritin up again, iron is working. Lipids, CMP fine. HIV and hep C negative.
Plan: cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg by mouth daily (sent to pharmacy; vegan formulations are easy to find). Recheck B12 in 3-6 months, at the latest with next physical. Continue iron. Pap pending.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap smear is normal. Routine schedule from here; we will talk about timing at your next physical. Enjoy the end of the school year.

documents.title: Stomach getting worse
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, since the start of the school year my stomach has gotten worse. Up to 5 or 6 loose BMs a day, sometimes a little blood, cramping on the right side, and I've lost about 5 lbs. I'm still taking the mesalamine every day. My GI appointment isn't until the end of November. Should I be doing something sooner?

documents.title: RE: Stomach getting worse
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. I have sent a note to your GI office asking them to move you up or call you about a plan in the meantime; please also call them directly today since they manage the mesalamine. If you have a fever, can't keep fluids down, have a lot of blood, or the pain becomes severe, go to the ED. Update: I spoke with GI - the date you hold is their soonest colonoscopy slot, you are on their cancellation list, and their nurse will call you about a plan until then.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines. Afebrile, feels OK aside from her bowels (GI aware, colonoscopy late November). Flu quadrivalent IM L deltoid; Pfizer bivalent COVID booster IM R deltoid. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 min, no reaction.

conditions.label: Crohn disease
conditions.note: Colonic skip lesions, granulomas, perianal fistula; initially labeled ulcerative colitis

medications.sig: Take 8 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily, then decrease by 1 tablet each week until off

reports.text: Indication: worsening diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss in a patient carrying a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. Moderate sedation. Prep adequate. Perianal inspection: external opening of a draining fistula. Scope advanced to the cecum and terminal ileum. Discontinuous areas of inflamed mucosa with erythema and ulceration in the colon, separated by segments of normal-appearing mucosa. Biopsies from inflamed and normal-appearing segments.
reports.conclusion: Patchy colitis with intervening normal mucosa and a perianal fistula, favoring Crohn disease. Biopsies sent.

reports.text: A-D. Colon, multiple sites, biopsies: chronic active colitis, patchy, with noncaseating granulomas in two of four sites; intervening biopsies with minimal change. No dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Chronic active colitis with noncaseating granulomas, consistent with Crohn disease.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up and colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP VISIT
Date of service: 11/29/2022

Ms. Shapiro returns, last seen here June 2021 for what was labeled left-sided ulcerative colitis, with iron deficiency anemia since diagnosed by her PCP in November 2021.

She reports six months of intermittent abdominal pain and diarrhea with steady weight loss, much worse over the last two months: up to six loose stools daily, sometimes with blood. Taking mesalamine 800 mg TID reliably, plus iron and B12.

FH: father with Crohn disease. SH: former smoker, quit 2020.

Exam: afebrile. Weight down from last visit. Abdomen: tender in the right lower quadrant, no rebound or guarding. Perianal exam: a draining fistula.
Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 9.5, CRP 24 mg/L, ESR 40.
Colonoscopy today: skip areas of inflamed colon between normal segments; perianal fistula. Pathology 12/2: noncaseating granulomas.

Impression: Crohn disease of the colon with perianal fistula. The earlier picture read as ulcerative colitis; with skip lesions, granulomas and fistulizing disease, we are revising the diagnosis to Crohn disease.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 40 mg daily, decrease 5 mg each week to off over 8 weeks.
2. Start infliximab 5 mg/kg IV (weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks) - preferred with the fistula. Before the first dose we need QuantiFERON, hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody; we have asked her PCP's office to draw these. Recommend inactivated vaccines (pneumococcal, recombinant zoster) before starting; no live vaccines on therapy.
3. Continue mesalamine 800 mg TID for now.
4. Continue oral iron and B12.
5. Return 2-3 months after induction.

Allergies: NKDA.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI request: pre-biologic labs
documents.author: RN
documents.body: GI nurse called: pt starting infliximab early January, asks us to draw QuantiFERON, HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs, results faxed to them. Also asking for pneumococcal and Shingrix before first infusion if possible. Orders entered per PCP. Called pt - coming tomorrow AM for labs, will book nurse visit for vaccines.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture R antecubital, one attempt. QuantiFERON tubes shaken and kept at room temp per protocol, sent with courier. Hep B panel sent. Pt tolerated well. Results to be faxed to GI on return.

documents.title: Nervous about infliximab
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doctor, honestly I'm a little freaked out. Crohn's like my dad, and now an IV drug every two months. I read about infections and lymphoma. Did my tests come back OK? Is it safe for me to be around 25 seven-year-olds all winter? The prednisone is helping already, which is good.

documents.title: RE: Nervous about infliximab
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very understandable to feel this way. Your TB test and hepatitis B tests are fine - no TB exposure, no hepatitis B, and you are immune from your childhood shots; GI has the results. Infliximab is a standard and effective treatment for Crohn disease with a fistula, and the serious risks are uncommon; GI will go over them in detail. Classroom life is fine. Hand-washing, your yearly flu shot (done) and COVID boosters (done) help, and you should call us with any fever. Next step here: the pneumonia vaccine and the first shingles shot at a nurse visit next week, both non-live and safe before infliximab. We are here for questions anytime.

documents.title: PCV20 and Shingrix #1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pre-infliximab vaccines per PCP and GI. On prednisone taper (now 35 mg). Afebrile. PCV20 IM L deltoid. Shingrix dose 1 IM R deltoid. Explained sore arm/fatigue for 1-2 days possible with Shingrix. Dose 2 due in 1-2 months; she will get it at her February visit. No reaction during 15-min observation.

medications.sig: 5 mg/kg IV infusion at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks

documents.title: Infusion center: infliximab induction summary
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
IBD INFUSION CENTER - INDUCTION SUMMARY
Patient: Deborah Shapiro
Drug: infliximab 5 mg/kg IV (400 mg, dosed on weight 78 kg)
Doses: #1 01/05/2023, #2 01/19/2023, #3 02/16/2023. Each infused over 2 hours with standard premedication per center protocol.
Screening on file: QuantiFERON negative 12/2022; HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive, anti-HBs reactive.
Tolerance: no infusion reactions. Vital signs stable before, during and after each infusion.
Maintenance: every 8 weeks; next infusion 04/13/2023.
Allergies: NKDA.
Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Insurance letter
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Letter from her PPO received by fax: prior authorization for infliximab approved by the plan through January 2024, requested by GI. Scanned to chart. No action needed from us; FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Infusion #2
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Second infusion done yesterday, no problems, just tired from sitting there 2+ hours. Bathroom trips are way down already. Do I need a note for school for the half-days on infusion days? The next one is a Thursday in February.

documents.title: RE: Infusion #2
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wonderful to hear. Yes - a letter for your principal stating you need medical leave for scheduled infusions every 8 weeks is attached; let me know if they need a different format.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective: here after the Crohn diagnosis change and first two infliximab infusions (third due 2/16). Prednisone taper finished around January 24. Stools now 1-2 a day and formed, no blood for about a month, no cramping. Gained back some weight. No infusion problems. Still on iron, B12, mesalamine.

Objective: vitals as charted, afebrile. Well. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft and nontender. No rash on the legs.

Assessment/Plan:
Crohn disease - doing well on infliximab after steroid course, managed by GI.
Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and ferritin today.
B12 deficiency on supplement - recheck at the physical.
On a biologic - Shingrix #2 today completes the series; PCV20 done. Labs today include liver tests.
F/u at physical late summer.

documents.title: Refills: ferrous sulfate, vitamin B12
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx renewal requests from her pharmacy for ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily and cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily. Both active, last visit 2/7/23. Sent 90-day supplies x 3 refills per PCP standing order.

orders.reason: Tender shin nodules in a patient with Crohn disease

documents.title: Acute visit: shin nodules
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: sore red lumps on both shins x3 days.

Started suddenly on Monday, a couple at first, now more. Tender to touch and with pants rubbing. No injury, no new meds or products, no fever. Bowels fine. Last infliximab mid-April, next early June.

Exam: afebrile. Several tender, warm, erythematous nodules on the anterior lower legs bilaterally, none ulcerated. No joint swelling. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P: tender shin nodules in a Crohn patient on infliximab - suspect erythema nodosum, want dermatology to confirm and look for other triggers. Referral sent as urgent. Leg elevation, cool compresses, avoid tight pants in the meantime. Messaged GI as FYI. Call if fever, ulceration or spreading redness.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs clear. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. Heart size normal. No pleural effusion. Bones unremarkable.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY CONSULT
Visit date: June 5, 2023
Reason for referral: tender nodules, lower legs

History: 29-year-old woman with Crohn disease (originally labeled ulcerative colitis) and iron deficiency anemia. Two weeks of painful red bumps on the shins that came on abruptly and have multiplied. No travel, no sick contacts, no new sexual partners. Her bowel disease is quiet on infliximab and mesalamine.
Medications: mesalamine DR 800 mg three times daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily; infliximab every 8 weeks (GI).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father Crohn disease, mother rheumatoid arthritis, paternal aunt hypothyroidism.
Social: does not smoke.

Exam: vital signs normal. Multiple 2-3 cm tender erythematous subcutaneous nodules over both anterior lower legs. No ulceration. No joint swelling. Abdomen nontender.

Workup: WBC 9.0, Hgb 13.2, ESR 40, CRP 2.5 mg/dL, ASO titer negative. Chest x-ray normal - no hilar adenopathy.

Assessment: erythema nodosum. No streptococcal, pulmonary or drug trigger identified; occurring alongside inflammatory bowel disease.

Plan: supportive care - rest, leg elevation, compression stockings when up and about. Lesions typically settle over 3-6 weeks without scarring. Her GI team should know, as flares of the skin and gut can travel together. Return if recurrent or ulcerating.

Dermatology

documents.title: Leg update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update - the bumps on my legs are fading, they look like old bruises now and barely hurt. Derm said that's how it goes. Summer break is helping, I can put my feet up!

documents.title: RE: Leg update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is exactly how they should fade. Thanks for letting me know. See you at your physical in August.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT, age 30

Summer was good - taught a week of art camp, otherwise resting. Bowels normal on infliximab every 8 weeks plus mesalamine. No bleeding, no abdominal pain, weight back up. The shin nodules from June are fully gone, no new ones. Taking iron and B12 daily. Mood good. No smoking. Alcohol rare.

Meds: infliximab q8 weeks (GI infusion), mesalamine DR 800 mg TID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Healthy-appearing. HEENT clear, no oral lesions. Neck supple. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass. Perianal deferred (GI following). Skin: shins clear, no nodules or discoloration; no suspicious moles on a quick look. No joint swelling.

A/P:
- Crohn disease, in remission on infliximab - GI follows.
- Erythema nodosum - resolved.
- Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and iron today.
- B12 deficiency, dietary - level today on supplement.
- On immunosuppression: flu and updated COVID vaccine in the fall (nurse visit). PCV20 and Shingrix complete. Pap 2022 normal; plan cervical screening again in 2025.
- Labs: CBC, ferritin/iron, B12, CMP.
RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news on your labs: blood count is normal now, iron stores are adequate, B12 is back in a healthy range on the supplement, and your kidney and liver tests are normal. Keep taking iron and B12 as you are. Have a great start to the school year.

documents.title: Seasonal vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent, IM L arm) and 2023-24 COVID (Pfizer, IM R arm) given. On infliximab - inactivated/mRNA vaccines only, confirmed. Afebrile. Observed 15 minutes, fine. Pt mentions some looser stools the last couple of weeks; advised to let GI know.

documents.title: Bumps are back + stomach
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The red bumps on my shins came back last week, same as in June. And for about 6 weeks my stomach has been off again - diarrhea, cramping, and I've lost weight (about 10 lbs?). I had my infusion on schedule. Should I go back to derm or GI or you?

documents.title: RE: Bumps are back + stomach
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: This sounds like a Crohn flare with the skin coming along for the ride, so GI is the right first stop - I have messaged them this morning and asked for a prompt visit. documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 11/29/2023
Dx: Crohn disease of the colon with perianal fistula (diagnosis revised from ulcerative colitis 11/2022), on infliximab 5 mg/kg q8 weeks since 01/2023.

Interval history: the shin nodules have returned over the past 3 weeks, and for 2 months she has had intermittent abdominal pain and diarrhea with an unintentional loss of 5 kg. Infusions on time.

Exam: tender erythematous nodules, 2-3 cm, over the anterior shins. Abdomen: right lower quadrant tenderness, no rebound or guarding.

Data: Hgb 10.2, MCV 72, CRP 24 mg/L, ESR 45, fecal calprotectin 250 ug/g. Stool culture and C. diff toxin (sent 11/22) negative.

Assessment: Crohn flare with recurrent erythema nodosum, with partial loss of response on standard-interval infliximab. Microcytic anemia, iron deficiency again with the flare.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 40 mg daily, taper by 5 mg weekly.
2. Shorten infliximab to every 6 weeks at 5 mg/kg, beginning with the next infusion; prior auth submitted.
3. Continue mesalamine 800 mg TID.
4. Continue oral iron and B12; PCP to recheck CBC after the flare.
5. Clinic in 3 months.

Medications reviewed: mesalamine DR 800 mg TID; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily; infliximab (infusion center).
Allergies: NKDA.

Gastroenterology

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Conjunctivae pink. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Legs: shins clear.

Impression and plan:

- Erythema nodosum - resolved again.
- Iron deficiency anemia with flare - CBC and iron today; continue oral iron.
- B12 on supplement.
Next: physical in late summer; sooner if flare.

documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY - RETURN VISIT
DOS 5/17/2024

Ms. Shapiro is a 30-year-old with Crohn disease, seen here in June 2023 for erythema nodosum, with another episode last fall during a Crohn flare. She now has six weeks of painful, deep nodules on the lower legs with low-grade fevers, joint aches and occasional fatigue. The spots came on abruptly and are tender enough that jeans and long walks are uncomfortable. No insect bites, no medication changes, no new skin products. About a month ago she had a sore throat and cough that cleared without treatment.

Meds: infliximab every 6 weeks, mesalamine, ferrous sulfate, cyanocobalamin. NKDA.

Exam: BMI 29. Several poorly demarcated, warm, erythematous plaques and subcutaneous nodules along the anterior shins; some are beginning to fade with a yellowish tinge. Oral and genital mucosa clear. No active joint swelling.

Rapid strep antigen in clinic: negative.

Assessment: recurrent erythema nodosum, likely related to her inflammatory bowel disease; the preceding throat illness may have contributed, though strep testing is negative now.

Plan: supportive care as before (elevation, compression, rest). Lesions in the fading stage should keep resolving over the next few weeks. Will copy GI. Return as needed.

Dermatology

No smoking since 2020. Alcohol rare. Vegan, on B12.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Skin: shins clear. Joints without synovitis.

A/P:
1. Preventive: Pap 2022 normal - co-test next year. Flu and COVID vaccines at an October nurse visit. Tdap good until 2026.
2. Crohn disease on infliximab - quiet; GI follows.
3. Erythema nodosum - resolved.
4. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and iron today.

6. Labs: CBC, iron studies, B12, CMP.
Follow-up in about 6 months.

conditions.label: Small bowel obstruction due to fibrotic stricture secondary to Crohn disease

reports.text: Supine and upright views of the abdomen. Multiple dilated loops of small bowel with air-fluid levels on the upright view. Little gas in the colon. No free air under the diaphragm. No abnormal calcifications.
reports.conclusion: Dilated small bowel with air-fluid levels, consistent with small bowel obstruction.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast. Findings: dilated, fluid-filled proximal and mid small bowel leading to a short narrowed segment of the distal ileum, beyond which the bowel is decompressed. The narrowed segment shows no mural hyperenhancement. No abscess, no fluid collection, no free air, no pneumatosis. Liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys and adrenals unremarkable. No adenopathy. Uterus and ovaries unremarkable. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Small bowel obstruction with transition at a short distal ileal stricture without active inflammatory features, consistent with a fibrotic Crohn stricture. No abscess or perforation.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 05/22/2025 06:40

HPI: 31 y/o F with Crohn disease, originally diagnosed as ulcerative colitis, on infliximab and mesalamine, presenting with 2 days of escalating abdominal pain with nausea and repeated vomiting, now green. No flatus and no stool since this began. No prior abdominal surgery.

PMH: Crohn disease; iron deficiency anemia; B12 deficiency; erythema nodosum.
Meds: mesalamine DR 800 mg TID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily; infliximab infusions.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: pack a day for 10 years by her account; quit in 2020. Alcohol rare.
FH: father Crohn disease.

Exam: T 37.8 C. Uncomfortable, actively retching. Abdomen distended, diffusely tender, bowel sounds hyperactive; no peritoneal signs. No hernias.

ED course: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, CRP 25 mg/L; BMP and lipase unremarkable; urine hCG negative. Abdominal films: dilated small bowel with air-fluid levels. NG tube placed with bilious return, IV fluids, antiemetic and IV analgesia. CT A/P: obstruction at a short fibrotic-appearing distal ileal stricture, no abscess or perforation. Surgery consulted in the ED.

Impression: small bowel obstruction from a Crohn stricture.
Disposition: admitted to medicine with surgery and GI following.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/22/2025  Discharged: 05/25/2025
Principal diagnosis: small bowel obstruction due to fibrotic stricture of the distal ileum, secondary to Crohn disease
Other: Crohn disease on infliximab; iron deficiency anemia; vitamin B12 deficiency
Procedures: none (no surgery)

Course: managed nonoperatively with nasogastric decompression, IV fluids and bowel rest. General surgery saw her on admission and agreed with nonoperative care. GI consulted: CT appearance is a fibrotic rather than inflammatory stricture, so no steroids; infliximab schedule unchanged. NG output fell over the first day; she passed flatus on hospital day 2 and stool on day 3. NG removed, clear liquids then low-residue diet advanced without vomiting or pain. Discharged home on day 4.

Discharge medications (unchanged): mesalamine DR 800 mg three times daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily; infliximab every 6 weeks per GI infusion schedule.
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: low-residue diet for now, chew well, avoid raw skins, seeds and nuts. Return for vomiting, distension, inability to pass gas or severe pain.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; GI as scheduled.

Hospital medicine

TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admission 5/22-5/25 at a regional hospital for small bowel obstruction at a fibrotic distal ileal stricture from Crohn disease. Nonoperative: NG tube, fluids, bowel rest. ED and discharge records reviewed (received 5/28). No medication changes at discharge.

Since home: eating low-residue, small portions, no vomiting. Daily soft BMs, passing gas, no cramping. Back at school as of Monday; tired at the end of the day. Lost a couple of pounds in the hospital.

Meds reconciled: infliximab q6 weeks (GI), mesalamine DR 800 mg TID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P:
1. Small bowel obstruction from Crohn stricture - resolved. Stay on low-residue diet; return precautions reviewed again (vomiting, bloating, no gas). GI aware; she sees them in the fall.
2. Crohn disease - continue current regimen per GI.
3. Anemia history - CBC today with BMP after the vomiting.
Physical in September.

Interval history: May admission for small bowel obstruction from an ileal stricture, managed without surgery. Since then no obstructive symptoms; she has loosened the low-residue diet carefully and tolerates it. Crohn otherwise quiet on infliximab q6 weeks and mesalamine. No leg nodules in over a year. GI visit with colonoscopy scheduled for November.
Well otherwise. Still vegan, on B12 and iron. Former smoker. PHQ-9 1.

Plan:

- Labs: CBC, iron studies, B12, CMP, lipids.
- Vaccines: flu and COVID in October; Tdap due next year.
- Crohn disease with prior stricture: per GI; return precautions known.

reports.text: Indication: Crohn disease, assessment of disease activity on infliximab. Moderate sedation. Prep good. Perianal inspection unremarkable. Scope advanced to the cecum; the ileocecal valve was traversed and the terminal ileum examined over a short distance. Mucosal inflammation is reduced compared with prior studies. Biopsies taken from the colon.
reports.conclusion: Reduced mucosal inflammation compared with prior colonoscopies. Biopsies sent.

reports.text: A-C. Colon, biopsies: colonic mucosa with decreased lamina propria lymphocytic infiltrate and less active inflammation than in prior specimens. No granulomas. No dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Decreased lamina propria inflammation; no granulomas or dysplasia.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up and colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GI FOLLOW-UP / COLONOSCOPY
DOS 11/17/2025

Reason: assessment of Crohn disease after the May 2025 admission for small bowel obstruction (fibrotic distal ileal stricture, managed nonoperatively).

History: this has been a hard few years for her - flares needing two prednisone courses and infliximab, with the interval shortened to every 6 weeks in 11/2023. Over the past year she has done much better: bowel movements normal, no abdominal pain, no obstructive symptoms since discharge.

Meds: mesalamine DR 800 mg TID; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily. (Infliximab at our infusion center.)
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father Crohn disease; mother RA; paternal aunt hypothyroidism.
SH: former smoker, rare alcohol, teacher.

Colonoscopy today: inflammation reduced compared with previous studies.
Pathology (11/20): decreased lamina propria lymphocytic infiltrate compared with prior specimens; no granulomas, no dysplasia.

Impression: Crohn disease with improving mucosal inflammation on infliximab every 6 weeks; history of fibrotic ileal stricture with obstruction, currently asymptomatic.

Plan:
- Continue infliximab 5 mg/kg every 6 weeks and mesalamine 800 mg TID.
- Call promptly for bloating, vomiting, or inability to pass gas.
- Clinic follow-up in 6 months.

Gastroenterology

Doing well. Crohn disease quiet: one to two normal BMs a day, no blood, no cramping, no bloating or vomiting since last May's admission. No skin nodules. Infliximab every 6 weeks at the GI infusion center (last one 3 weeks ago), mesalamine three times a day, iron and B12 daily - occasionally forgets the midday mesalamine. GI visit planned for May. Energy good; teaching a spring mural project. Still not smoking.

Meds: infliximab 5 mg/kg IV q6 weeks (GI), mesalamine DR 800 mg TID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily. Allergies: none known.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Conjunctivae pink. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nondistended, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Shins clear. No edema.

1. Crohn disease, quiet on infliximab and mesalamine; prior ileal stricture without symptoms. Continue per GI.
